G5300.def:
ὗς, ὑός, ὁ, ἡ
[in LXX for חֲזִיר ;] 
swine: fem. (sow), 2 Pierre 2:22,†

G5301.def:
ὕσσωπος, -ου, ἡ 
[in LXX for אֵזוֹב ;] 
hyssop, of which a bunch was used in ritual sprinklings: Hébreux 9:19; of a branch or rod (?) of hyssop, Jean 19:29 (but see Field, Notes, 106 ff., for suggestion to substitute ὑσσῷ here).†

G5302.def:
ὑστερέω, -ῶ
(ὕστερος), [in LXX for חָסֵר, חָדַל etc. ;] 
to come late, be behind (opposite to προτερέω, φθάνω; with genitive of thing(s), for; with genitive of person(s), later than). 
Metaphorical, 
__1. of persons, 
__(a) absol., to come short, fail: Hébreux 4:1; before ἀπό, Hébreux 12:15.; 
__(b) with genitive of person(s), to come short of, be inferior to: 2 Corinthiens 11:5; οὐδέν (in nothing, in no respect), 2 Corinthiens 12:11; 
__(with) with reference to things, to come short (of ), be in want (of ): with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 19:20 (Sir.51:24); with genitive of thing(s), Luc 22:35; so mid. (Diod., FlJ), Romains 3:23; absol., to be in want, suffer want, Luc 15:14, 1 Corinthiens 8:8, 2 Corinthiens 11:8, Hébreux 11:37 (Sir.11:11); opposite to περισσεύειν, Philippiens 4:12; before ἐν, 1 Corinthiens 1:7. 
__2. Of things, 
__(a) to fail, be lacking: Jean 2:3; with accusative of person(s) (see Swete, in l; Mozley, Psaumes 42:1-11), Marc 10:21; 
__(b) to be inferior: mid., 1 Corinthiens 12:24 (cf. ἀφ-υστερέω).†

G5303.def:
ὑστέρημα, -τος, τό
(ὑστερέω), [in LXX: Juges 18:10 19:19-20, Psaumes 34:9 (מַחְסוֹר), Ecclésiaste 1:15 (חֶסְרוֹן), Esther 6:9 (ὑ. εἶναι, חֲשַׁח) * ;] 
__(a) that which is lacking, deficiency, shortcoming: with genitive puss. (prop. pose.), 1 Corinthiens 16:17, Philippiens 2:30; with genitive of thing(s), Colossiens 1:24, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:10; 
__(b) need, want, poverty (Psaumes 34:10, Juges 18:10, al.): Luc 21:4, 2 Corinthiens 9:12 11:9; opposite to περίσσευμα, 2 Corinthiens 8:13-14 (eccl.).†

G5304.def:
ὑστέρησις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑστερέω), [in Aq.: Job 30:3 * ;] 
need, want: opposite to τὸ περισσεῦον, Marc 12:44; καθ᾽ ὑ., Philippiens 4:11 (eccl.).†

G5306.def:
ὕστερος, -α, -ον 
[in LXX for אַחֲרוֹן and cogn. forms ;] 
latter, later: ἐν ὑ. καιροῖς, 1 Timothée 4:1 (on the reading ὁ ὕ., WH, for ὁ πρῶτος, see WH, App., in l). Neut., τὸ ὕ., used adverbially instead of ὑστέρως, afterwards, later: Matthieu 4:2 21:29, 32 21:37 25:11 26:60, Marc 16:14, Luc 20:32, Jean 13:36, Hébreux 12:11; with genitive, Matthieu 22:27.†

G5307.def:
ὑφαντός, -ή, -όν
(ὑφαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב ;] 
woven: Jean 19:23.†
ὑφαίνω, 
[in LXX for אָרַג, etc. ;] 
to weave: Luc 12:27, T, WH, mg.†

G5308.def:
ὑψηλός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּמָה, also for בָּמָה, רוּם, etc. ;] 
high, lofty: ὄρος, Matthieu 4:8 17:1, Marc 9:2, Apocalypse 21:10; τεῖχος, Apocalypse 21:12; μετὰ βραχίονος., figuratively, Actes 13:17 (cf. Exode 6:6, al); pl., ὑψηλά, of heaven (Psaumes 93:4, Ésaïe 33:5, al.), Hébreux 1:3; compar., ὑψηλότερος τ. οὐρανῶν, Hébreux 7:26. Metaph: Luc 16:15; ὑψηλὰ ψρσνεῖν, Romains 11:20 12:16, 1 Timothée 6:17 (WH, txt., ὑψηλοφρονείν).†

G5309.def:
ὑψηλο- φρονέω, -ῶ 
= μευαλοφρονεῖν (Xen., Plat., al.), 
to be high-minded: 1 Timothée 6:17 (WH, mg., ὑψηλὰ, φρονεῖν).†

G5310.def:
ὕψιστος, -η, -ον superlat., without positive in use, in cl. chiefly poët. (Æsch., Soph., al.), 
[in LXX chiefly for עֶלְיוֹן, also for מָרוֹם, etc. ;] 
highest, most high: of place, τὰ ὕ. (of the heavens), Matthieu 21:9, Marc 11:10, Luc 2:14 19:38 (cf. Joshua 16:19, Ésaïe 57:15); of God (in cl., of Zeus; Pind., Æsch., al.), ὕ., Luc 1:32, 35 1:76 6:35 (as frequently in Sir.4:10, al.); ὁ ὕ., Actes 7:48; ὁ θεὸς ὁ ὕ., Marc 5:7, Luc 8:28, Actes 16:17, Hébreux 7:1 (cf. Genèse 14:18).†

G5311.def:
ὕψος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX for קוֹמָה, מָרוֹם, etc. ;] 
height: Éphésiens 3:18 Jacques 1:9, Apocalypse 21:16; of heaven (EV, on high), ἐξ ὕ., Luc 1:78 24:49; εἰς ὕ., Éphésiens 4:8 (LXX)†

G5312.def:
ὑψόω, -ῶ
(ὕψος), [in LXX chiefly for רוּם, also for גָּבַהּ, נָשָׂא, etc. ;] 
to lift or raise up: with accusative, Jean 3:14 8:28 12:32, 34; ἕως τ. οὐρανοῦ, figuratively, pass., Matthieu 11:23, Luc 10:15. Metaphorical, to exalt, uplift: Actes 2:33 5:31, 2 Corinthiens 11:7, Jacques 4:10, 1 Pierre 5:6; opposite to ταπεινῶ, Luc 1:52; ἑαυτόν, Matthieu 23:12, Luc 4:11 18:14 (cf. ὑπερ-υψόω).†

G5313.def:
ὕψωμα, -τος, τό 
[in LXX: Job 24:24 (†), Jdth.10:8 13:4 15:9 * ;] 
__(a) height: Romains 8:39; 
__(b) that which is lifted up, a barrier: 2 Corinthiens 10:5.†

G5314.def:
φάγος, -ου, ὁ
(φαγεῖν, see: ἐσθίω) 
a glutton: Matthieu 11:19, Luc 7:34.†

G5315.def:
φάγομαιHellenistic for cl. ἔδομαι, see: ἐσθίω.
ἐσθίω, and (poet, and late prose) ἔσθω, 
[in LXX chiefly for אכל ;] 
to eat; 
__(a) absol.: Matthieu 14:20, 21 Marc 6:31, Jean 4:31, al.; ἐν τ. φαγεῖν (on this aor. form, see M, Pr., 111), 1 Corinthiens 11:21; διδόναι φαγεῖν, with dative of person(s), Marc 5:43, al.; ἐ. καὶ πίνειν, Matthieu 6:25, 31 Luc 10:7, al.; of ordinary use of food and drink, 1 Corinthiens 9:4 11:22; of partaking of food at table, Marc 2:16, Luc 5:30, al.; opposite to fasting, Matthieu 11:18, Luc 5:33, al.; of revelling, Matthieu 24:49, Luc 12:45 . 
__(b) with accusative of thing(s): Matthieu 6:25, Marc 1:6, Jean 6:31, Romains 14:2, al.; ἄρτον (Heb. אָכַל לֶחֶם), Matthieu 15:2, Marc 3:20, al.; τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ἄ., 2 Thessaloniciens 3:12; ἄ. before παρά, genitive of person(s), 2 Thessaloniciens 3:8; τά before id., Luc 10:7; τ. πάσχα, Matthieu 26:17, Marc 14:12 al; τ. κυριακὸν δεῖπνον, 1 Corinthiens 11:20; τ. θυσίας, 1 Corinthiens 10:18; before ἐκ (= cl. part. genitive), Jean 6:26, 5o, 51, 1 Corinthiens 11:28; ἀπό (cf. Heb. אָכַל מִן), Matthieu 15:27, Marc 7:28; metaphorically, to devour, consume: Hébreux 10:27, Jacques 5:3, Apocalypse 17:16 (cf. κατ-, συν-εσθίω) .

G5316.def:
φαίνω
[in LXX for אוֹר hi., רָאָה ni., etc. ;] 
__I. Act., 
__1. to bring to light, cause to appear (so most frequently in cl.). 
__2. Absol., to give light, shine (Hom., Plat., al.): Jean 1:5 5:35, 2 Pierre 1:19, 1 Jean 2:8, Apocalypse 1:16 8:12 18:23 21:23. 
__II. Pass., to come to light, appear, be manifest: Matthieu 2:7 13:26 24:27, 30, Luc 9:8, Philippiens 2:15, Hébreux 11:3, 1 Pierre 4:18" (LXX) ; opposite to ἀφανίζεσθαι, Jean 4:14; with dative of person(s) (Bl. § 54, 4), Matthieu 1:20 2:13, 19 Marc 16:9; with nom. pred., Matthieu 23:27-28, Romains 7:13, 2 Corinthiens 13:7; id. with dative of person(s), Matthieu 6:5, 16 6:18 (before nom. ptcp., but not as in cl.; see Bl., § 73, 4); impers., Matthieu 9:33; of the mind and judgment (= δοκεῖ, which see), Marc 14:64 (cf. I Esther 2:21), Luc 24:11.†
SYN.: see: δοκέω

G5317.def:
Φάλεκ (T, Rec. Φαλέκ, L, mg., Φάλεγ), ὁ indecl. (Heb. D, Ge 1116), 
Peleg: Luc 3:35.†

G5318.def:
φανερός, -ά, -όν
(φαίνομαι) [in LXX: Deutéronome 29:29 (28) (גָּלָה ni.), Proverbes 14:4, Sir.6:22, al. ;] 
open to sight, visible, manifest: Galates 5:19; before ἐν, Romains 1:19, 1 Jean 3:10; with dative of person(s), Actes 4:16 7:13, 1 Timothée 4:15; φ. γίνεσθαι (in LXX for בָּחַן ni., Genèse 42:16), Marc 6:14, Luc 8:17, 1 Corinthiens 3:13 14:25; id. before ἐν, 1 Corinthiens 11:19, Philippiens 1:13; φ. ποιεῖν, Matthieu 12:16, Marc 3:12; εἰς φ. ἐλθεῖν (cf. Bl., § 47, 2), Marc 4:22, Luc 8:17; ἐν τῷ φ. (opposite to ἐν τ. κρυπτῷ), Romains 2:28.†
SYN.: see: δῆλος

G5319.def:
φανερόω, -ώ 
[in LXX: Jérémie 40:6 (33:6) (גָּלָה pi.) * ;] 
to make visible, clear, manifest or known: with accusative of thing(s), Jean 2:11 17:6, Romains 1:19, 1 Corinthiens 4:5, 2 Corinthiens 2:14 11:6, Colossiens 4:4, Tite 1:3; pass., Marc 4:22, Jean 3:21 9:3, Romains 3:21 16:26, 2 Corinthiens 4:10-11, Éphésiens 5:13, Colossiens 1:26, 2 Timothée 1:10, Hébreux 9:8, 1 Jean 3:2 Jn 4:9, Apocalypse 3:18 15:4; with accusative of person(s), of Christ, Jean 7:4 21:1; pass., 2 Corinthiens 3:3 5:10-11, 1 Jean 2:19; of Christ, Marc 16:12, 14, Jean 1:31 21:14, Colossiens 3:4, 1 Timothée 3:16, Hébreux 9:26, 1 Pierre 1:20 5:4, 1 Jean 1:2 (ἡ ζωή; see Westc., in l) 1 Jean 2:28 Jn 3:2 Jn 3:5 Jn 3:8.†
SYN.: see: ἀποκαλύπτω

G5320.def:
φανερῶς
adv. (φανερός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:28 * ;] 
__(a) manifestly, openly: Marc 1:45; opposite to ἐν κρυπτῷ„ Jean 7:10; 
__(b) clearly: Actes 10:3 (2Ma.3:28).†

G5321.def:
φανέρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(φανερόω), [in LXX as seel. for δήλωσις אוּרִים), Lévitique 8:8, Cod. Ven. (Thayer, see word) * ;] 
manifestation: 1 Corinthiens 12:7, 2 Corinthiens 4:2.†

G5322.def:
φανός, -οῦ, ὁ
(φαίνω), 
a torch or lantern (see Rutherford, NPhr., 131 f.): Jean 18:3.†
SYN.: see: λαμπάς

G5323.def:
Φανουήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. פְּנוּאֵל), 
Phanuel: Luc 2:36.†

G5324.def:
φαντάζω
(φαίνω) [in LXX: Wis.6:16, Sir.31:5 (34:5)* ;] 
to make visible. In cl. used in pass. only, = φαίνομαι, to become visible, appear: ptcp., Hébreux 12:21.†

G5325.def:
φαντασία, -ας, ἡ
(φαντάζω), [in LXX: Zacharie 10:1 (חֲזִיז), חֲזִיז), Habacuc 2:18-19 3:10, Wis.18:17 * ;] 
__1. as philos. term, 
__(a) imagination; 
__(b) = φάντασμα (Plat., Arist.). 
__2. In later writers (Polyb., al.), show, display: Actes 25:23.†

G5326.def:
φάντασμα, -τος, τό
(φαντάζω), [in LXX: Job 20:8 A (חִזָּיוֹן), Ésaïe 28:7 A, Wis.17:15 * ;] 
= φάσμα, an appearance, apparition (Æsch., al.): Matthieu 14:26, Marc 6:49 (see DCG, i, 111b).†

G5327.def:
φάραγξ, -αγγος, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for נַחַל, also for גַּיְא, etc. ;] 
a chasm, ravine: Luc 3:5 (LXX) (see DB, iv, 845 f.).†

G5328G.def:
Φαραώ, ὁ indecl. 
(in FlJ, Ant., viii, 6, 2, Φαραών, -ῶνος), (Heb. פַּרְעֹה), 
Pharaoh, the general title of the kings of Egypt: Actes 7:13, 21, Romains 9:17, Hébreux 11:24; Φ. βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, Actes 7:10.†

G5328H.def:
Φαραώ, ὁ indecl. 
(in FlJ, Ant., viii, 6, 2, Φαραών, -ῶνος), (Heb. פַּרְעֹה), 
Pharaoh, the general title of the kings of Egypt: Actes 7:13, 21, Romains 9:17, Hébreux 11:24; Φ. βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, Actes 7:10.†

G5328I.def:
Φαραώ, ὁ indecl. 
(in FlJ, Ant., viii, 6, 2, Φαραών, -ῶνος), (Heb. פַּרְעֹה), 
Pharaoh, the general title of the kings of Egypt: Actes 7:13, 21, Romains 9:17, Hébreux 11:24; Φ. βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, Actes 7:10.†

G5329.def:
Φαρές, ὁ indecl. (Heb. פֶּרֶץ, Genèse 38:29), 
Peres: Matthieu 1:3, Luc 3:33.†

G5330.def:
Φαρισαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. פְּרִישָׁא; see Dalman, Gr., 157.n, Words, 2.n), 
a Pharisee: Matthieu 23:26, Philippiens 3:5; usually in pl., Matthieu 9:11, Marc 2:18, al.; Φ. κ. γραμματεῖς, Matthieu 5:20, Marc 2:16, Luc 5:21, al.; Φ. κ. Σαδδυκαῖοι, Matthieu 16:1, Actes 23:6, 7 al.; ἀρχιερεῖς, Matthieu 21:45, Jean 7:32, al. (see DB, iii, 826b).

G5331.def:
φαρμακία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ
(φαρμακεύω, to administer drugs) 
poët. and late prose form of φαρμακεία, 
[in LXX: Exode 7:11, 22 8:7, 18 (3, 14) (לָט, חַרְטֹם), Ésaïe 47:9, 12 (כֶּשֶׁף) Wis.12:4 18:13 * ;] 
__1. generally, the use of medicine, drugs or spells (Xen.). 
__2. (a) poisoning (Plut., Polyb.); 
__(b) sorcery, witchcraft: Galates 5:20 (see Lft., in l), Apocalypse 9:21 (WH, txt., φαρμάκων) Apocalypse 18:23 (cf. LXX, ll. with).†

G5333.def:
φαρμακός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX for כָּשַׁף, etc. ;] 
devoted to magical arts. As subst., ὁ φ. = φαρμακεύς, a magician, sorcerer: Apocalypse 21:8 22:15.†

G5334.def:
φάσις, -εως, ἡ
(φαίνω), [in LXX: Esther 4:17, Da TH Su 1:55, 4Ma.15:25 א1 * ;] 
information, esp. against fraud or other crime: Actes 21:31.†

G5335.def:
φάσκω 
[in LXX: Genèse 26:20 (אָמַר), Dan LXX Bel 1:8, 2Ma.14:27 2Mac 14:32, 3Ma.3:7 * ;] 
to affirm, assert: with accusative and inf., Actes 24:9 25:19; with inf. and nom., Romains 1:22.†

G5336.def:
φάτνη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX for אֵבוּס, etc. ;] 
a manger: Luc 2:7, 12 2:16 13:15 (see DB, iii, 234a, DCG, ii, 111a),†

G5337.def:
φαῦλος, -η, -ον 
[in LXX: Proverbes 22:8 (עֶוֶל) Proverbes 29:9 (אֱוִיל), etc. ;] 
slight, worthless, of no account, both of persons and things in various shades of meaning (see LS, see word), in NT, as frequently in cl., always with distinct moral reference (see Ellic., Past. Epp., 203; Hort, Ja., 85; Tr., Syn., LXXxiv), worthless, bad: Jean 3:20, Tite 2:8, Jacques 3:16; opposite to ἀγαθός (which see), Jean 5:29, Romains 9:11, 2 Corinthiens 5:10.†
SYN.: see: ἄθεσμος

G5338.def:
φέγγος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for נֹגַהּ ;] 
light, brightness, usually with genitive of something that shines or reflects: of the moon, Matthieu 24:29, Marc 13:24; of a lamp, Luc 11:33 (WH, RV, φῶς).†
SYN.: αὐγή, q.v

G5339.def:
φείδομαι 
[in LXX for חָמַל, חוּס, חָשַׂךְ, etc. ;] 
to spare: 2 Corinthiens 13:2; with genitive of person(s), Actes 20:29, Romains 8:32 11:21, 1 Corinthiens 7:28, 2 Corinthiens 1:23, 2 Pierre 2:4-5; with inf., to forbear, 2 Corinthiens 12:6.†

G5340.def:
φειδομένως 
adv. from ptcp. (see 131., § 25, 1), 
sparingly: 2 Corinthiens 9:6 (Plut.).†

G5341.def:
φελόνης (Rec. φαιλ-), -ου, ὁ 
by metath. for παινόλης (also φενόλης, φαινόλιον; Lat. pænula) 
a cloak (see DCG, i, 338; on the idea that the meaning here is book-cover, see CGT, in l; Milligan, NTD, 20; Field, Notes, 217 f., where the view that the φ. here is an eccl. vestment is discussed): 2 Timothée 4:13.†

G5342.def:
φέρω 
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא. hi., also for נָשָׂא, etc. ;] 
to bear; 
__1. to bear, carry: with accusative, Luc 23:26 24:1, Jean 19:39, Hébreux 1:3 (see Westc., in l); pass., Actes 2:2 27:15, 17 Hébreux 6:1, 2 Pierre 1:17-18; of the mind, 2 Pierre 1:21. 
__2. to bear, endure: with accusative of thing(s), Hébreux 12:20 13:13; with accusative of person(s), Romains 9:22. 
__3. to bring, bring forward: with accusative of person(s), Actes 5:16; id. before πρός, Marc 1:32 2:3 9:17, 19-20; ἐπί, Luc 5:18; with dative, Marc 7:32 8:22; with accusative of thing(s), Marc 6:27 11:2 12:15, Luc 15:23, Actes 4:34, 37 5:2, 2 Timothée 4:13; id. before πρός, Marc 11:7; εἰς, Apocalypse 21:24, 26; ἐπί, Matthieu 14:11, Marc 6:28; ἀπό, Jean 21:10; with dative, Marc 12:15, Jean 2:8; id. before ὧδε, Matthieu 14:18 17:17; before φαγεῖν (sc. τι), Jean 4:33; τ. δάκτυλον (χεῖρα), Jean 20:27; pass., ἡ χάρις, 1 Pierre 1:13; διδαχήν, II Jn 10; θάνατον (cf. Field, Notes, 230), Hébreux 9:16; κρίσιν, 2 Pierre 2:11; κατηγορίαν, Jean 18:29; αἰτίαν, Actes 25:18; αἰτιώματα, Actes 25:7, Rec. 
__4. to bear, produce, bring forth: καρπόν, Matthieu 7:18, Marc 4:8, Jean 12:24 15:2, 4-5 15:8, 16. 
__5. to bring, lead: Marc 15:22, Jean 21:18, Actes 14:13; metaphorically, of a gate (ὁδός, cl.), Seq. εἰς, Actes 12:10 
(cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, εἰσ-, παρ-εισ-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, -παρα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ὑπο-φέρω).† 
SYN: φορέω, which expresses habitual and continuous bearing as distinct from (φέρω) that which is accidental and temporary (cf. Matthieu 11:8, al., see word φορέω, and see Tr., Syn., § lviii)

G5343.def:
φεύγω 
[in LXX chiefly for נוּס, also for בָּרַח, etc. ;] 
to flee from or away, take flight: absol., Matthieu 8:33 26:56, Marc 5:14 14:50, Luc 8:34, Jean 10:12, Actes 7:29; before εἰς, Matthieu 2:13 10:23 24:16 (WH, txt.), Marc 13:14, Luc 21:21, Apocalypse 12:6; ἐπί, with accusative loc., Matthieu 24:16 (WH, mg.); ἐκ, Actes 27:30; ἀπό, with genitive loc. (cl.), Marc 16:8; id. with genitive of person(s) (as in Heb.), Jean 10:5, Jacques 4:7. Metaphorical: absol., Apocalypse 16:20; with accusative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 6:18, Hébreux 11:34 (see M, Fr., 116); opposite to διώκειν, 1 Timothée 6:11, 2 Timothée 2:22; before άπό, with genitive of person(s), Apocalypse 9:6; άπὸ τ. προσώπου, Apocalypse 20:11; with genitive of thing(s), Matthieu 3:7 (M, Pr., l.with) Matthieu 23:33, Luc 3:7, 1 Corinthiens 10:14 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, κατα-φεύγω).†

G5344.def:
φῆλιξ (L, Φή-), -ικος, ὁ
Felix, procurator of Judæa: Actes 23:24, 26 24:3, 22 24:24-25, 27 25:14.†

G5345.def:
φήμη, -ης, ἡ
(φημί) [in LXX: Proverbes 16:2 (15:30) (שְׁמוּעָה), 2Ma.4:39, 3Ma.3:2, 4Ma.4:22 * ;] 
a saying or report: Matthieu 9:26, Luc 4:14.†

G5346.def:
φημί 
[in LXX chiefly for נָאַם, also for אָמַר; frequently in 2-4 Mac ;] 
to declare, say: frequently in quoting the words of another, Matthieu 13:29 26:61, Luc 7:40 22:58, Jean 1:23, al.; interjected into the recorded words (cl.), Matthieu 14:8, Actes 23:35, al.; φησί, impersonal (Bl., § 30, 4), 1 Corinthiens 6:16 (Lft., Notes, 217; but cf. Bl., l.with), 2 Corinthiens 10:10 (WH, mg., φασίν), Hébreux 8:5; joined with syn. verb (cf. LS, see word, II, 2), ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη, Luc 23:3; before -πρός, Luc 22:70, al.; with accusative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 10:15 10:19; accusative and inf., Romains 3:8; before ὅτι (Bl., § 70, 3), 1 Corinthiens 10:19 15:50 (cf. σύν-φημι)

G5347.def:
φῆστος, -ου, ὁ
(Porcius), Festus, procurator of Judæa: Actes 24:27 25:1 ff. Actes 26:24-25, 32.†

G5348.def:
φθάνω 
[in LXX for נָגַע hi., מְטָא, etc. ;] 
__1. to come before another, anticipate (cl.): with accusative of person(s), 1 Thessaloniciens 4:15. 
__2. In late writers and MGr. (see Kennedy, Sources, 156; Lft., Notes, 35), to come, arrive: Romains 9:31; before εἰς, Philippiens 3:16; ἄχρι, 2 Corinthiens 10:14; ἐπί (cf. Da TH Daniel 4:21, and see Dalman, Words, 107), Matthieu 12:28, Luc 11:20, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:16 (cf. προ-φθάνω).†

G5349.def:
φθαρτός, -ή, -όν (φθείρω) 
[in LXX: Lévitique 22:25 (מִשְׁחָת), Ésaïe 54:17 A א3, Wis.9:15 14:8, 2Ma.7:16 * ;] 
perishable, corruptible: ἄνθρωπος, Romains 1:23 (opposite to ἄφθαρτος θεός); στέφανος, 1 Corinthiens 9:25 (opposite to αρτος); σπσρά, 1 Pierre 1:23 (opposite to ἄφθ.); neut., τὸ φ. τοῦτο, 1 Corinthiens 15:53-54; pl., 1 Pierre 1:18.†

G5350.def:
φθέγγομαι 
[in LXX for עָנָה, נָבַע hi., etc. ;] 
of men or animals, to utter a sound or voice: absol., Actes 4:18; before ἐν φωνῇ, 2 Pierre 2:16; with accusative, ὑπέρογκα, 2 Pierre 2:18.†

G5351.def:
φθείρω 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת hi., pi., also for חָבַל, etc. ;] 
to destroy, corrupt, spoil (on the varied usage and distinctive meaning of the word, see Mayor on 2Pe, App., 175 ff.): with accusative, 1 Corinthiens 3:17 15:23, 2 Corinthiens 7:2; before ἀπό, 2 Corinthiens 11:3; ἐν, 2 Pierre 2:12, Ju 10, Apocalypse 19:2; κατά, Éphésiens 4:22 (cf. δια-, κατα-φθείρω).†

G5352.def:
φθιν-οπωρινός, -ή, -όν
(φθινόπωρον, late autumn), 
autumnal: δένδρα φ., autumn trees (said to be without fruit therefore at a time when fruit might be expected; see Mayor's elaborate note, Ep. Ju., 55-59, and reff. there): Ju 12.†

G5353.def:
φθόγγος, -ου, ὁ
(φθέγγομαι), [in LXX: Psaumes 19:4 (קַו), Wis.19:18 * ;] 
a sound: Romains 10:18 (LXX) 1 Corinthiens 14:7.†

G5354.def:
φθονέω, -ῶ
(φθόνος), [in LXX: Tob.4:7, 16 AB * ;] 
to envy: with dative (L, txt., Tr., mg., WH, mg., accusative), as in cl., Galates 5:26.†

G5355.def:
φθόνος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Wis.2:24 6:23, 1Ma.8:16, 3Ma.6:7 * ;] 
envy: Romains 1:29, Galates 5:21, 1 Timothée 6:4, Tite 3:3, 1 Pierre 2:1; διὰ φθόνον, Matthieu 27:18, Marc 15:10, Philippiens 1:15; πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τ. πνεῦμα (on the meaning, see R, txt., mg. 1, 2; Hort, Ja., 93 f.), Jacques 4:5.†

G5356.def:
φθορά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(φθείρω) [in LXX for שַׁחַת, חֶבֶל, etc. ;] 
destruction, corruption, decay (see Mayor on 2Pe, App.,175 ff.): Romains 8:21, 1 Corinthiens 15:42, Colossiens 2:22, 2 Pierre 2:12; opposite to ζωὴ αἰώνιος, Galates 6:8; by meton., of that which is subject to corruption, 1 Corinthiens 15:50; of moral decay, 2 Pierre 1:4 2:12 2:19 (cf. Wis.14:12).†

G5357.def:
φιάλη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for מִזְרָק ;] 
a shallow bowl (= Lat. patera), used for pouring libations, etc.: Apocalypse 5:8 15:7 16:1-17 17:1 21:9.†

G5358.def:
φιλ-άγαθος, -ον 
[in LXX: Wis.7:22 * ;] 
loving that which is good, loving goodness: Tite 1:8 (Arist., Polyb., a l.).†

G5359.def:
Φιλαδελφία (Rec. -έλφεια), -ας, ἡ 
Philadelphia, a city of Lydia: Apocalypse 1:11 3:7.†

G5360.def:
φιλαδελφία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλάδελφος), [in LXX: 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 13:26 4Mac 14:1 * ;] 
the love of brothers, brotherly love: of Christians' mutual love as brethren (see: ἀδελφός), Romains 12:10, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:9, Hébreux 13:1, 1 Pierre 1:22, 2 Pierre 1:7.†

G5361.def:
φιλ-άδελφος, -ον 
[in LXX: 2Ma.15:14, 4Ma.13:21 4Mac 15:10 * ;] 
loving one's brother, loving like a brother (Soph., Xen., al.): of Christians' love for one another (EV, loving as brethren), 1 Pierre 3:8.†

G5362.def:
φίλανδρος, -ον 
__1. loving men (Æsch.). 
__2. Of a wife, loving her husband (frequently in epitaphs, see LS, see word, Deiss., BS, 255): Tite 2:4.†

G5363.def:
φιλανθρωπία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλάνθρωπος, humane), [in LXX: Esther 8:13, 2Ma.6:22 2Mac 14:9, 3Ma.3:15 3Mac 3:18 * ;] 
humanity, kindness (see Field, Notes, 147 f.): Actes 28:2, Tite 3:4 (cf. also DCG, ii, 356 ff.).†

G5364.def:
φιλανθρώπως 
adv., [in LXX: 2Ma.9:27, 3Ma.3:20 * ;] 
humanely, kindly: Actes 27:3.†

G5365.def:
φιλαργυρία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλάργυρος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 2:15 א1 * ;] 
love of money, avarice: 1 Timothée 6:1.†
SYN.: πλεονεξία, covetousness (see Tr., Syn., § xxiv)

G5366.def:
φιλ-άργυρος, -ον 
[in LXX: 4Ma.2:8 * ;] 
loving money, avaricious: Luc 16:14, 2 Timothée 3:2.†

G5367.def:
φίλ-αυτος, -ον 
loving oneself (Arist.); in bad sense (ib.), selfish: 2 Timothée 3:2.†
SYN.: αὐθάδης (see Tr., Syn., § xciii)

G5368.def:
φιλέω, -ῶ
(φίλος), [in LXX: Genèse 27:4, 9, al. (אָהַב), Genèse 27:27, al. (נָשַׁק), La 1:2 (רֵעַ) Wis.8:2, al. ;] 
__1. to love (with the love of emotion and friendship, Lat, amare; v, SYN.): with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 10:37, Jean 5:20; Jean 11:3, 36 15:19 16:27 20:2 21:15-17, 1 Corinthiens 16:22, Apocalypse 3:19; ἐν πίστει, Tite 3:15; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 23:6, Luc 20:46, Jean 12:25, Apocalypse 22:15; with inf. (Ésaïe 56:10; cf. Bl., § 69, 4), Matthieu 6:5. 
__2. to kiss: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 26:48, Marc 14:44, Luc 22:47 (cf. κατα-φιλέω).†
SYN.: ἀγαπάω ω (which see), the love of duty and respect

G5369.def:
φιλήδονος, -ον
(φίλος, ἡδονή), 
loving pleasure: 2 Timothée 3:4 (Polyb., Plut. al.).†

G5370.def:
φίλημα, -τος, τό
(φιλέω), [in LXX: Proverbes 27:6, Cantique des cantiques 1:2 (נְשִׁיקָה) * ;] 
a kiss: Luc 7:45 22:48; as a token of Christian brotherhood, φ. ἅγιον, Romains 16:16, 1 Corinthiens 16:20, 2 Corinthiens 13:12, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:26; φ. ἀγάπης, 1 Pierre 5:14 (see Lft., Notes, 90; DB, DCA, see word "Kiss").†

G5373.def:
φιλία, -ας, ἡ
(φίλος), [in LXX chiefly for אַהֲבָה ;] 
friendship: with genitive obj., Jacques 4:4.†

G5374.def:
φιλιππήσιος, -ου, ὁ
(for other forms in use, see Lft., in l) 
a Philippian: Philippiens 4:15.†

G5375.def:
φίλιπποι, -ων, οἱ
(on the pl., see WM, § 27, 3) 
Philippi: Actes 16:12 20:6, Philippiens 1:1, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:2.†

G5376G.def:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ 
Philip; 
__1. the husband of Herodias: Matthieu 14:3, Marc 6:17. 
__2. The tetrarch: Matthieu 16:13, Marc 8:27, Luc 3:1. 
__3. The apostle: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:14, Jean 1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Actes 1:13. 
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Actes 6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†

G5376H.def:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ 
Philip; 
__1. the husband of Herodias: Matthieu 14:3, Marc 6:17. 
__2. The tetrarch: Matthieu 16:13, Marc 8:27, Luc 3:1. 
__3. The apostle: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:14, Jean 1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Actes 1:13. 
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Actes 6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†

G5376I.def:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ 
Philip; 
__1. the husband of Herodias: Matthieu 14:3, Marc 6:17. 
__2. The tetrarch: Matthieu 16:13, Marc 8:27, Luc 3:1. 
__3. The apostle: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:14, Jean 1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Actes 1:13. 
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Actes 6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†

G5376J.def:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ 
Philip; 
__1. the husband of Herodias: Matthieu 14:3, Marc 6:17. 
__2. The tetrarch: Matthieu 16:13, Marc 8:27, Luc 3:1. 
__3. The apostle: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:14, Jean 1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Actes 1:13. 
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Actes 6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†

G5376K.def:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ 
Philip; 
__1. the husband of Herodias: Matthieu 14:3, Marc 6:17. 
__2. The tetrarch: Matthieu 16:13, Marc 8:27, Luc 3:1. 
__3. The apostle: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:14, Jean 1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Actes 1:13. 
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Actes 6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†

G5378.def:
1. fond of speaking , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. fond of learning, literary , Lat. studiosus, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G5379.def:
φιλονεικία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλόνεικος), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 8:26 * ;] 
love of strife, rivalry, emulation (Plat., al.), but mostly in bad sense (Thuc., al.), contentiousness, contention: Luc 22:24 (but see Field, Notes, 75 f.).†

G5380.def:
φιλό-νεικος, -ον
(νεῖκος, strife) [in LXX: Eze.3:7 (חָזָק ־מֵצַח)* ;] 
fond of strife, contentious: 1 Corinthiens 11:16.†

G5381.def:
φιλο-ξενία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλόξενος), 
love of strangers, hospitality: Romains 12:13, Hébreux 13:2.†

G5382.def:
φιλό-ξενος, -ον 
loving strangers, hospitable: 1 Timothée 3:2, Tite 1:8, 1 Pierre 4:9.†

G5383.def:
φιλο-πρωτιύω
(φιλόπρωτος, Plut., al.) 
to strive to be first: III Jn 9 (eccl.).†

G5385.def:
Φιλο-σοφία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλόσοφος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:1 4Mac 5:10 4Mac 5:22 4Mac 7:9 4Mac 7:21 * ;] 
the love and pursuit of wisdom; hence, philosophy, investi­gation of truth and nature: of the so-called philosophy of false teachers, Colossiens 2:8 (see Lft., ICC, in l).†

G5386.def:
φιλό-σοφος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Dan LXX 1:20 (אַשָּׁף), 4Ma.1:1 4Mac 5:35 4Mac 7:7 * ;] 
a philosopher: Actes 17:18.†

G5387.def:
φιλόστοργος, -ον
(στοργή, family affection), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:13 * ;] 
tenderly loving, affectionate (Xen., Plut., al.): of Christians, Romains 12:10.†

G5388.def:
φιλότεκνος, -ον
(φίλος, τέκνον), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:4-6 * ;] 
loving one's children (Hdt., Arist., Plut., al.): of women, joined with φίλανδρος, which see, Tite 2:4.†

G5389.def:
φιλοτιμέομαι, -οῦμαι
(φίλος, τιμή), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:35 A ;] 
to love or seek after honour, hence, to be ambitious, emulous (Plat., Plut., al.): with inf., Romains 15:20, 2 Corinthiens 5:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:11.†

G5390.def:
φιλοφρόνως
(φιλόφρων) 
adv., [in LXX: 2Ma.3:9, 4Ma.8:5 * ;] 
kindly, with friendliness: Actes 28:7.†

G5392.def:
φιμόω, -ῶ
(φιμός, a muzzle), [in LXX: Deutéronome 25:4 (חָסַם), Dan LXX Su 1:61, 4Ma.1:35 א R * ;] 
to muzzle: 1 Corinthiens 9:9, 1 Timothée 5:18" (LXX) ; metaphorically, to put to silence: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 22:34, 1 Pierre 2:15; pass., to be silenced, silent: Matthieu 22:12, Marc 1:25 4:39, Luc 4:35.†

G5394.def:
φλογίζω
(φλόξ), [in LXX: Exode 9:24 (לָקַח hith.), Nombres 21:14 (†), Psaumes 97:3 (לָהַט pi.), Da TH Daniel 3:27(94) (חָרַךְ ithp.), Sir.3:30, 1Ma.3:5 * ;] 
to set on fire, burn, burn up: figuratively, Jacques 3:6 (on the meaning of the sentence, see Hort, in l).†

G5395.def:
φλόξ genitive, φλογός, 
[in LXX chiefly for לַהַב, לֶהָבָה ;] 
a flame: Luc 16:24; φ, πυρός, Actes 7:30, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:8, Hébreux 1:7" (LXX), Apocalypse 1:14 2:18 19:12.†

G5396.def:
φλυαρέω, -ῶ
(φλύαρος), 
to talk nonsense: with accusative of person(s), ἡμᾶς (EV, prating against us), III Jn 10.†

G5397.def:
φλύαρος, -ον
(φλύω, to babble), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:10 * ;] 
babbling, garrulous: 1 Timothée 5:13 (EV, tattlers; of things, φιλοσοφία, 4Mac, l.with).†

G5398.def:
φοβερός, -ά, -όν
(φοβέω), [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵא, also for דְּחַל, אָיֹם ;] 
fearful, whether act, or pass.; 
__1. act., = δεινός, causing fear, terrible (LXX): Hébreux 10:27, 31 12:21 
__2. Pass., = δειλός, feeling fear, timid (cl. in both senses).†

G5399.def:
φοβέέω, ῶ
(φόβος) [in LXX chiefly for מִן יָרֵא ;] 
__1. in Hem., to put to flight. Pass., to be put to flight, to flee affrighted 
__2. to terrify, frighten (Wis 179; Hdt. and Att..). Pass. (so always in NT; cf. M, Pr., 162), to be seized with fear, be affrighted, fear: Matthieu 10:31 14:27, Marc 5:33 6:50, Luc 1:13 8:50, Jean 6:19 12:15, Actes 16:38, al.; opposite to ὑψηλοφρονεῖν, Romains 11:20; σφόδρα, Matthieu 17:6 27:54; with cogn. accusative, φόβον μέγαν, Marc 4:41, Luc 2:9 (1Ma.10:8); φόβον αὐτῶν (obj, genitive, but cf. ICC, in l), 1 Pierre 3:14; πτόησιν, 1 Pierre 3:6; with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 10:26, Marc 11:18, Luc 19:21, Jean 9:22, Actes 9:26, 
Romains 13:3, al.; before ἀπό (like Heb. יָרֵא, Jérémie 1:8, al.; cf. M, Pr., 102, 104n„), Matthieu 10:28, Luc 12:4; before μή (cl.; Bl., § 65, 3; M, Pr., 184 f.), Actes 23:10 27:17; μήπως, Actes 27:29, 2 Corinthiens 11:3 12:20, Galates 4:11; μήποτε, Hébreux 4:1; with inf. (Bl., § 69, 4; M, Pr., 205), Matthieu 1:20, Marc 9:32, al.; of reverential fear: Marc 6:20, Éphésiens 5:33; τ. θεόν, Luc 1:50, Actes 10:2, 1 Pierre 2:17, Apocalypse 14:7, al.; τ. κύριον, Colossiens 3:22, Apocalypse 15:4; τ. ὄνομα τ. θεοῦ (see: ὄνομα), Apocalypse 11:18; οἱ φοβούμενοι τ. θεόν, of proselytes, Actes 13:16, 26 (cf. ἐκ-φοβέω)
